answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work to the bridge; rewards accrue only after independent peers verify its output, while proven fraud burns the stake. This makes a sybil attack costly: splitting one identity into many does not multiply influence without multiplying capital, and fake agents that fail verification lose their deposits. An atlas of past attestations can guide peer selection, but reputation alone cannot replace the bond; even a ferrous badge is just a label, not proof of uniqueness.
